content.title: About
content.content: Green leaf tea is made from unoxidized leaves of Camellia sinensis. It has a light, fresh flavor with herbal notes and a mild bitterness. The tea is usually brewed with water at 70‑80 °C for 2‑3 minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green tea is one of the most consumed beverages worldwide, especially in China and Japan.
The leaves are not fermented, which preserves more polyphenols than black tea.
Traditional Japanese "matcha" is powdered green tea used in tea ceremonies.
In Japan the "Hanami" festival celebrates cherry blossoms while enjoying green tea.
There are over 300 varieties of green tea, differing by growing region and processing method.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Green tea contains catechins, especially EGCG, which help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Regular consumption may help lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Boosts metabolism
items.content: Caffeine and catechins increase fat oxidation, which can aid weight management.

items.title: Enhances brain function
items.content: The combination of caffeine and L‑theanine improves alertness and concentration.

items.title: May reduce risk of certain diseases
items.content: Studies link green tea intake with lower risk of some cancers and type‑2 diabetes.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High amounts can cause nervousness, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Green tea may enhance the effects of anticoagulants and some blood‑pressure medications.

items.title: Tannin content
items.content: Tannins can reduce iron absorption from plant foods, so people with anemia should drink tea between meals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place 1‑2 tsp of leaves in hot (not boiling) water, steep for 2‑3 minutes, then strain. You may add lemon, honey, or ginger to taste. For a cold version, chill the brew and serve over ice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store green leaf tea in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep it away from moisture and strong odors to preserve flavor and beneficial compounds.
